featured_reviews.name: vishal kudtarkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
First Car Experience Ruined – False Promises & Huge Financial Loss

This was my first car purchase, and unfortunately, it turned into one of the worst buying experiences of my life.

I saw the car in the first week of January 2025. Since I was a first-time buyer and not fully aware of technical details, I trusted the dealer. I paid a token amount after they promised delivery within a couple of weeks and assured me that all issues like minor dents, polishing, AC work, clutch work, etc. would be fully resolved before delivery.

On the delivery day, the car was nowhere near ready. Shockingly, no work had been done at all even after taking the token. Only when I arrived in the morning did they start working on the car. I had to wait the entire day and finally got delivery at 8:30 PM, which is unacceptable.

Within one week, the engine check light came on. The car started overheating and had issues with the crankshaft sensor and timing belt. I contacted them immediately. They asked me to give the car for “2 days,” which turned into 10–12 days. I had to keep calling repeatedly with no clear response.

Even after that, the car still had issues. They assured me that since the ownership transfer was not done yet, I could use the car for 15 days and they would replace it if problems continued. After those 15 days, the situation became worse—the car barely gave 5 kmpl, despite being promised 13–15 kmpl.

When checked at another workshop, I was informed the engine had major back compression issues, with repair estimates of ₹1.3–1.5 lakh. After this, the dealer became unreachable, saying the office was closed or that they were out of town—for 1–2 months.

Left with no choice, I sold the car and suffered a loss of nearly 45% of the purchase amount within just a few months.

After this entire experience, I did some research on my own and noticed that the dealer has a workshop located on the opposite side of the road from the showroom. From what I could observe and understand, many cars appear to be worked on there—repaired, repainted, and fixed for defects—before being sold.

This explains why their pricing is slightly lower compared to other dealers. However, these cars are presented as being in excellent or “ready” condition, while in reality they seem to be heavily worked-on vehicles rather than genuinely problem-free ones.

As a customer, this lack of transparency is extremely concerning, especially for first-time buyers who trust the dealer’s word.

This was my first and last car from this dealership. I’m sharing this review so others don’t go through the same stress, time loss, and financial damage.

When I contacted a senior representative to discuss these concerns, the first question I was asked was how I obtained his number, which was disappointing. Only after I mentioned escalating the matter to Tata Motors did the conversation become constructive.

I don't mind paying for quality service, but I expect transparency, proper communication, customer approval before additional work is carried out, and resolution of reported issues. Unfortunately, my experience has been far below expectations.

featured_reviews.name: Anirban Ghosh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Positive Service Experience with a Key Process Improvement Opportunity

⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)

I recently visited Indrajit Cars, Mira Road for the second service of my Tata Punch.

The appointment was honoured as scheduled, and I also received a reminder call a day prior, which was a professional and reassuring touch. I chose to wait at the service centre while the work was being carried out. I handed over the car at around 10 AM and received it by approximately 2 PM. While the overall process was smooth, for a second service with a prior appointment, I feel the turnaround time could possibly be quicker.

The staff was polite, respectful, and courteous throughout the interaction. However, communication can be improved, especially for customers who may not have extensive experience with car servicing. A clearer explanation of what is typically included in a second service would be helpful, rather than the customer having to ask proactively.

There was no add-on or forced selling at all, which I genuinely appreciated. In terms of service quality, the work done was very good, and I’m happy with how the car performs after the service. All concerns I mentioned at the time of handover were documented and explained as resolved during billing. That said, I strongly feel the final handover should include a practical demonstration of the fixes done. This gives customers confidence that their concerns were truly heard and addressed. For customers who wait at the service centre for the entire duration, this should ideally be a standard practice rather than something they need to verify later on their own.

The waiting experience will naturally vary based on individual preferences. Personally, my expectations are simple—a clean and comfortable space—and on that front, the service centre met them well. The area was clean and equipped with basic amenities such as air conditioning, television, newspapers, and drinking water.

Overall, a positive service experience with good service quality, along with a clear opportunity to strengthen the final customer assurance process.

Would I return? ✔ Yes
